title: Squared norm of the orthogonal component along a unit vector
statement:
Let $V$ be a real inner product space, let $u \in V$ be a unit vector, so $\norm{u} = 1$, and let $x \in V$ be arbitrary. Then
\[
\norm{x - \langle x, u\rangle\, u}^2 = \norm{x}^2 - \langle x, u\rangle^2 .
\]
hypotheses_covered: V is a real inner product space
x is an arbitrary vector of V
replaced:
For a unit vector $u$ and any $x$ in a real inner product space,
$\norm{x - \langle x,u\rangle u}^2 = \norm{x}^2 - \langle x,u\rangle^2$.
